Package io.github.brantunger.unruly.api

Class Rule

java.lang.Object
io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Rule
public class Rule extends Object
A Rule is an object that guides the RulesEngine. When the condition expression evaluates to true, the RulesEngine fires the action expression during execution of the RulesEngine.run(FactStore) method.

Fields:

  • ruleName: identifies the rule in error messages and listener callbacks. Must be unique within a rule list; a rule without a name is allowed.
  • condition: an expression that must evaluate to a boolean. It can't assign or declare anything. Required.
  • action: an expression run when the rule fires. It changes the output object, which it sees as output. Required.
  • priority: higher values fire first. Equal priorities keep their list order, and a null priority sorts last.
  • description: free text for your own use. The engine ignores it, but listeners receive it.
  • language: the name of the expression language the condition and action are written in, as registered with RulesEngine.registerLanguage(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.language.ExpressionLanguage). null, the default, means MVEL.

Create a rule with Rule.builder(), or with the no-arg constructor and setters, which is how JSON and configuration binders create one. Copy a rule with a change with toBuilder(), for example rule.toBuilder().priority(5).build(). The positional constructors are deprecated: their parameters change whenever a field is added.

Nullness: ruleName, priority, description and language are Nullable. condition and action are required, so they aren't, but a rule created with the no-arg constructor or a builder has neither until they are set, and RulesEngine.setRuleList(java.util.List) rejects it until then.

equals and hashCode compare every field, including description and language. A field added in a later release takes part too.

RulesEngine.setRuleList(java.util.List) takes a copy of each rule. Changing a Rule afterwards has no effect on the engine, including on what listeners and error messages report, until setRuleList is called again.

Security: conditions and actions are code. In MVEL, the default language, they have the same access to the JVM as Java code, including processes, files and reflection; what a rule in another language can reach depends on that language. The engine applies no sandbox and no timeout, so only use rules from trusted sources.
